Retatrutide (LY3437943): The GLP-1/GIP/Glucagon Triple Agonist Breaking Every Weight Loss Record — Research Dossier

Medical Disclaimer: Research compounds discussed for educational purposes only. Retatrutide is investigational and not FDA-approved anywhere as of November 2026. Not a treatment recommendation. Consult a healthcare provider before any clinical decision.

What Is Retatrutide?

Retatrutide (LY3437943) is an investigational once-weekly injectable peptide developed by Eli Lilly that simultaneously activates three receptors: the GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R), the GIP receptor (GIPR), and the glucagon receptor (GCGR). It is the world's first triple agonist to complete Phase 3 clinical trials and has produced the highest weight loss results ever recorded in a large-scale anti-obesity drug trial — up to 28.3% mean body weight reduction at 80 weeks.

To put that in context: average weight loss with Ozempic (semaglutide) in Phase 3 trials was approximately 15%. With Zepbound (tirzepatide) it was approximately 21%. With retatrutide, it reaches 25–28%. For some patients — 45.3% of TRIUMPH-1 participants on the 12 mg dose — weight loss exceeded 30%, approaching the typical range of bariatric surgery.

Mechanism of Action: Why Three Receptors?

Each of the three receptor targets contributes a distinct metabolic mechanism:

GLP-1 Receptor (GLP-1R)

The foundation of modern obesity pharmacotherapy. GLP-1R agonism slows gastric emptying, stimulates insulin secretion in a glucose-dependent manner, suppresses glucagon, and activates hypothalamic satiety circuits — reducing appetite and caloric intake. This is the shared mechanism with semaglutide and the cornerstone of the GLP-1 drug class.

GIP Receptor (GIPR)

The addition that made tirzepatide more effective than semaglutide. GIP receptor agonism augments incretin-mediated insulin secretion and may enhance GLP-1R signaling through receptor-level cross-talk. GIPR agonism also appears to have adipose-tissue-specific effects that complement GLP-1R activity in driving fat mass reduction. The success of tirzepatide validates the GLP-1R + GIPR combination — retatrutide builds on this.

Glucagon Receptor (GCGR)

The differentiator. Glucagon receptor agonism directly drives hepatic fat oxidation and thermogenesis, increasing the rate at which stored fat is burned even at rest. This mechanism operates independently of reduced caloric intake — it increases energy expenditure while GLP-1R and GIPR components reduce caloric intake. The combination of reduced intake (GLP-1R/GIPR) and increased fat burning (GCGR) is what distinguishes retatrutide's mechanism from every currently approved obesity drug.

The triple synergy explains why the weight loss magnitude — 25–28% — substantially exceeds both the GLP-1 mono (semaglutide, ~15%) and GLP-1/GIP dual (tirzepatide, ~21%) approaches.

TRIUMPH Phase 3 Program: 6 Positive Trials

TRIUMPH-1: Obesity (Without Type 2 Diabetes)

Topline announced May 21, 2026. Largest retatrutide obesity trial.

  • 12 mg weekly: mean body weight reduction ~25–28.3% at 80 weeks
  • 45.3% of 12 mg participants achieved ≥30% weight loss
  • Weight loss was still ongoing at 80 weeks in some analyses, suggesting full plateau had not been reached
  • Met primary endpoint and all key secondary endpoints

TRIUMPH-2: Type 2 Diabetes With Obesity

Topline announced July 23, 2026.

  • Mean weight reduction: 20.8% at 80 weeks
  • Significant A1C reduction; met all primary and key secondary endpoints

TRIUMPH-3: Severe Obesity With Cardiovascular Disease

Topline announced July 23, 2026.

  • Mean weight reduction: 22.6% at 80 weeks
  • MACE-5 hazard ratio: 0.82 (confidence intervals crossed 1.0 — cardiovascular benefit suggested but not conclusively established; no cardiovascular harm signal)

TRIUMPH Knee Osteoarthritis

Positive Phase 3 results for reduction in knee OA pain as an obesity-related comorbidity. The first obesity drug to demonstrate significant improvement in OA pain as a formal secondary indication.

TRIUMPH Obstructive Sleep Apnea

Positive Phase 3 results for sleep apnea severity reduction. Lilly said the full data package supports filing for obesity, knee OA pain, and OSA as indications.

TRANSCEND-T2D-2: Retatrutide Beats Ozempic Head-to-Head

Topline announced October 28, 2026 — the most recent pivotal data for retatrutide. This was the first prospective head-to-head trial of retatrutide versus a standard approved semaglutide dose.

Design: 1,298 adults with type 2 diabetes randomized 2:2:1 to retatrutide 9 mg, retatrutide 12 mg, or Ozempic (semaglutide) 2 mg weekly for 80 weeks. Ozempic 2 mg was chosen as the highest currently approved semaglutide dose for type 2 diabetes.

Outcome Retatrutide 12 mg Ozempic 2 mg
Mean weight change −20.9% (−47.4 lbs) −9.4% (−20.9 lbs)
A1C reduction −2.2% −1.8%

Retatrutide 12 mg produced more than double the weight loss of Ozempic 2 mg. This is the first published comparison of retatrutide versus any approved semaglutide dose in a randomized trial.

Key Research Findings

  • Up to 28.3% mean weight loss in TRIUMPH-1 (12 mg, 80 weeks) — highest ever in a Phase 3 anti-obesity drug trial
  • 45.3% of TRIUMPH-1 participants lost ≥30% body weight — a surgical-range threshold
  • TRANSCEND-T2D-2: more than 2× the weight loss of Ozempic 2 mg head-to-head (−20.9% vs. −9.4%)
  • 6 positive Phase 3 trials across obesity, type 2 diabetes, knee OA, and sleep apnea
  • Positive cardiovascular trend in TRIUMPH-3 (HR 0.82) but confidence intervals crossed 1.0 — awaiting CVOT data
  • Also effective for knee osteoarthritis pain and sleep apnea — multi-indication potential

Dosing in Clinical Trials

Retatrutide was administered as a once-weekly subcutaneous injection in all TRIUMPH trials:

  • Starting dose: typically 2 mg SC weekly, titrated over several weeks
  • TRIUMPH-1 tested doses including 4 mg, 8 mg, and 12 mg at maintenance
  • Weight loss was dose-dependent, with 12 mg producing the most dramatic effects
  • Dose escalation schedules were used to manage gastrointestinal tolerability
  • Retatrutide is investigational; doses outside of clinical trials are not approved or validated

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How does retatrutide differ from semaglutide and tirzepatide?

Retatrutide adds a third receptor target — the glucagon receptor — on top of the GLP-1R and GIPR targets that tirzepatide hits. Semaglutide targets only GLP-1R. Each additional receptor adds a different metabolic mechanism: GLP-1R provides satiety and glucose control; GIPR augments incretin effects; glucagon receptor drives direct hepatic fat oxidation and thermogenesis. The clinical result is progressively greater weight loss: semaglutide Phase 3 ~15%, tirzepatide Phase 3 ~21%, retatrutide Phase 3 25–28.3%. TRANSCEND-T2D-2 (October 28, 2026) showed retatrutide achieving more than double the weight loss of Ozempic 2 mg in type 2 diabetes. The head-to-head TRIUMPH-5 trial versus tirzepatide is ongoing, with results expected in late 2026 or early 2027.

Q: What does 28.3% weight loss in TRIUMPH-1 actually mean?

For a person starting at 250 lbs (113 kg), that's a loss of approximately 62–70 lbs on average. These figures are the highest ever reported in a Phase 3 anti-obesity drug trial. Perhaps more striking: 45.3% of TRIUMPH-1 participants on 12 mg lost ≥30% of body weight — approaching the typical range for bariatric surgery (25–35% at one year), suggesting that for many patients retatrutide can achieve pharmacologically what surgery achieves mechanically. Full peer-reviewed publications are pending.

Q: When will retatrutide be approved and available?

Eli Lilly announced plans to file a Biologics License Application (BLA) with the FDA in Q1 2027, with the data package supporting obesity, knee osteoarthritis pain, and obstructive sleep apnea. If FDA grants standard review, approval could come in late 2027 or early 2028. The drug is not approved anywhere as of November 2026 and is not available outside of clinical trials.

Research Limitations

  • Not FDA-approved; all TRIUMPH results are from topline company announcements pending full peer-reviewed publication
  • Cardiovascular outcomes trial: TRIUMPH-3 HR 0.82 with non-significant confidence intervals — cardiovascular benefit suggested but not established; dedicated CVOT not yet completed
  • TRIUMPH-5 head-to-head vs. tirzepatide pending — this will be the definitive comparison with the leading approved dual agonist
  • Gastrointestinal adverse events (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) are common during dose escalation; discontinuation rate modestly higher than placebo
  • Long-term safety profile (beyond 80 weeks) not yet established
  • Manufacturing and regulatory review timelines could affect actual approval date
Research Disclaimer: This content is for educational purposes only. Retatrutide (LY3437943) is an investigational compound with no regulatory approval anywhere as of November 2026. All efficacy and safety data are from preliminary topline company announcements pending peer-reviewed publication. No information here constitutes medical advice. Consult a physician before any clinical consideration.
